task.description: Security review of the new webhook-subscriptions route layer against security-invariants.md INV-1 through INV-8, focused on: (1) permission gating on all four routes including the newly-added PATCH clause, (2) cross-tenant-404 behavior (never 403) for PATCH/DELETE against another tenant's real subscription id, (3) the plaintext secret (hmac_secret_once) is emitted only once, on POST's own success response, and never via GET/list or any other response path, (4) secret_hash/tenant_id/__meta__ are never emitted by subscription_json/1.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions with no secret supplied returns a 2xx response whose body includes hmac_secret_once carrying the plaintext secret exactly once; a subsequent GET/list of the same subscription never includes the plaintext secret or an hmac_secret_once field at all
PATCH /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/:id accepts {status: "PAUSED"} and, separately, {is_active: false}, and both result in a subscription that subsequently reads back as PAUSED via GET/list

every subscription route requires the WebhooksManage permission from REQ-069's matrix -- a caller lacking it receives 403, and a caller from a different tenant naming a real subscription id belonging to tenant A receives 404, never 403
GET /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions returns {items: [...]} with each item's target_url, event_types, status and created_at present, matching webhooksApi.list's consumer shape
DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/:id removes the subscription such that a subsequent list no longer includes it, and a second DELETE of the same id returns 404 rather than a duplicate success
the route module's moduledoc states explicitly that R-Co's webhooks.zig was not inspected in this batch and that web/src/api/dlq.ts / web/src/types/api.ts were the binding contract instead
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary: All applicable invariants (INV-1, INV-2, INV-4, INV-5, INV-6, INV-7, INV-8) verified directly against the real diff and the real Letflow.Webhooks context module -- not trusted from the router's own moduledoc or the design doc's claims. INV-3 not applicable. PATCH clause in authorization.ex confirmed to map to the same :WebhookSubscriptionsManage -> :WebhooksManage permission as the other three routes, granted only to PLATFORM_ADMIN/PROCESS_OPERATOR. Cross-tenant probes on PATCH/DELETE fold :invalid_id and :not_found into one identical Response.not_found/1 call. secret_hash/tenant_id/__meta__ never emitted by subscription_json/1; hmac_secret_once appears only on the POST create-success branch. Routed to REVIEWER via handoffs/WF02-REQ182-20260829/step-02d-reviewer.json, flagging the known stale webhooks_test.exs structural assertion (expected, not a security issue) and stale S4-gating language in security-invariants.md's INV-2/INV-5 sections for follow-up.
